page: Amazon Web Services is4gen.large is a storage-optimized server instance powered by the AWS Nitro hypervisor. It features an ARM64-based AWS Graviton Neoverse-N1 processor with 2 dedicated physical cores running at a clock speed of 2.5 GHz. The hardware configuration includes 12.0 GB of system memory, providing a 1:6 vCPU-to-memory ratio, and a substantial 1875 GB local NVMe SSD storage volume. Network performance is rated at a baseline bandwidth of 3 Gbps.

Benchmark data reveals a clear tradeoff between storage capacity and raw processing power. While single-core CPU performance via stress-ng is average at 1519.59, multi-core CPU and memory bandwidth metrics fall into the weak to poor categories. For example, Geekbench multi-core scores of 1753.0 and Passmark memory scores of 1236.38 indicate limited computational throughput. Static web serving throughput is measured at 2.34 GB/sec, and LLM inference speeds for a small 135M model reach 22.98 tokens/sec for text generation.

From a cost-efficiency perspective, the is4gen.large offers high local NVMe storage density per vCPU, making it a specialized choice where storage capacity is prioritized over high-performance compute. It is poorly suited for CPU-intensive tasks, software compilation, or complex mathematical modeling. Instead, the instance is best utilized for workloads requiring significant local storage and moderate memory, such as localized databases, log indexing, and basic storage-heavy applications.
